Article 6 (Setting Monetary Policy Directions)
(1) The Bank of Korea shall set an inflation target in consultation with the government.
(3) The Bank of Korea shall do its best to achieve the inflation target as provided for in paragraph (1).

II. Monetary Policy Direction for 2011
The inflation target for the 2010-12 period is set at the level of 3.0 ± 1%, in terms of the year-on-year rate of increase in the Consumer Price Index.

The Bank of Korea ("the Bank") shall consequently conduct its monetary policy with the aim of ensuring that the rate of price increase stabilizes at the midpoint of this target range, from a medium-term perspective.

Market interest rates are forecast to come under mild upward pressure, influenced by the upbeat tone of economic activity, by upward price pressures, and so on.

In conducting monetary policy, the Bank will place emphasis on price stability, while taking into consideration changes in financial and economic conditions at home and abroad.
2. Enhancing the Efficient Conduct of Monetary and Credit
The Bank will work to enhance its capacity to adjust liquidity, by means such as improving the instruments used in its open market operations.

The Bank will also strive to improve its policy instruments and strengthen its communication, in order to heighten efficiency in its conduct of monetary policy, while at the same time redoubling its efforts directed toward financial system stability.

Systems for information exchange and cooperation with major central banks, international agencies and other bodies will be strengthened.

Furthermore, active participation in the discussions concerning financial stability, such as those on the construction of global financial safety nets, within the G20, the Financial Stability Board, the Basel Committee on Bank Supervision and other fora, will be pursued.
The drive for policy communication, both domestically and internationally, will be further stepped up through such means as provision of a more swift and accurate English-language service.
The Bank will also continue its efforts to reinforce the content of its Monetary Policy Report and Financial Stability Report, both of which are published twice a year.
In the area of inter-agency cooperation, the Bank, working together with the relevant authorities, will seek to firmly fix into place the various systems for enhancing macro-prudential soundness.
A detailed implementation plan will be prepared, in cooperation with the government, to ensure that 'Macro-prudential Stability Levies' are imposed in the 2nd half of 2011 as scheduled.
4. Strengthening the Efforts for Financial Stability
The Bank will constantly monitor factors with the potential to bring about financial instability, and strengthen its macro-prudential surveillance in this regard.
The Bank will also work to heighten the safety and efficiency of the payment and settlement systems.

The efforts to this end will include seamless implementation of the scheme for indirect provision of intraday liquidity to securities companies, and strengthening of the framework for efficient management of settlement risks.
To this end, the household sector's indebtedness, global financial market risk factors, foreign capital in- and outflows, geopolitical risks and so on will be vigilantly monitored at all times.
Checks on systemically important medium-size and large banks and on potentially vulnerable sectors will be tightened during the Bank's conduct of joint examinations.
In addition, analysis and appraisal of financial system stability will be refined, through for example the development of financial stability indicators and the improvement of stress testing models.
Efforts will also be redoubled to entrench the framework for information sharing and cooperation on financial stability with the government and the financial supervisory authorities.
